questions.q: What does summarize ... by ... combine into one operator?
options: groupBy() and .agg(), from Foundations Lessons 53 and 54
where and project
join and union
take and extend
questions.explain: by VendorID is the grouping; named aggregate expressions compute per group, just like agg().

questions.q: How does KQL's TripCount = count() differ in syntax order from PySpark's count("*").alias("trip_count")?
options: KQL writes name = expression; PySpark writes expression.alias(name) — the underlying statistical concept is identical
They compute completely different values
KQL cannot name its aggregate results at all
PySpark's alias() has no equivalent naming behavior in KQL
questions.explain: The order is flipped, but both name an aggregate result per group.

questions.q: What does bin(pickup_time, 1h) actually do to a timestamp?
options: Rounds it down to the nearest hour interval, so summarize can group events into real time buckets
Deletes the timestamp column entirely
Converts the timestamp to a string
Filters out any timestamp outside business hours
questions.explain: This is a genuinely new idea without a direct Foundations equivalent — the mechanism behind time-series aggregation.

questions.q: Why is summarize ... by bin(pickup_time, 1h) described as a genuinely different question from a batch groupBy()?
options: It groups a continuously arriving stream into hourly buckets as it arrives, updating live, rather than grouping a static, already-loaded DataFrame
There's no real difference between the two
bin() can only be used on batch data, never streaming data
groupBy() already supports time-bucketing identically
questions.explain: "How many trips happened in the 2 PM hour, updated live" is a streaming-native question.

questions.q: Which aggregate functions does summarize support, corresponding directly to Foundations Lesson 54's functions?
options: count(), sum(), avg(), max(), min()
Only count(), nothing else
Only functions unique to KQL with no PySpark equivalent
summarize does not support any aggregate functions
questions.explain: The underlying statistical concept is identical; only the calling syntax differs between the two languages.
